title: Shader Baker Does Not Bake All Sprite3D Shader Versions
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable
- The code appears to be the same on master.

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.rc (7160efa07) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7688) - AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.08 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

In `ShaderBakerExportPlugin::_customize_scene`, the logic attempts to find all Sprite3D in the scene, calculate which material/shader the Sprite3D will use, and bake the appropriate shader at compile time. It does this by closely mimicking the code that Sprite3D typically executes at runtime in `draw_texture_rect`.

This mostly works correctly, but the Shader Baker version only compiles the shader with "texture repeat" disabled. The Shader Baker code doesn't make any effort to detect whether the shader will or won't be used with texture repeat.

One fairly easy fix here is to simply compile the shader both with and without texture repeat enabled to cover all bases:
```
// This code is already present.
Ref<Material> sprite_3d_material = StandardMaterial3D::get_material_for_2d(bool(properties["shaded"]), mat_transparency, bool(properties["double_sided"]), billboard_mode == StandardMaterial3D::BILLBOARD_ENABLED, billboard_mode == StandardMaterial3D::BILLBOARD_FIXED_Y, false, bool(properties["no_depth_test"]), bool(properties["fixed_size"]), BaseMaterial3D::TextureFilter(int(properties["texture_filter"])), BaseMaterial3D::AlphaAntiAliasing(int(properties["alpha_antialiasing_mode"])));
_customize_resource(sprite_3d_material, String());

// Add this to also compile the texture repeat enabled version.
sprite_3d_material = StandardMaterial3D::get_material_for_2d(bool(properties["shaded"]), mat_transparency, bool(properties["double_sided"]), billboard_mode == StandardMaterial3D::BILLBOARD_ENABLED, billboard_mode == StandardMaterial3D::BILLBOARD_FIXED_Y, false, bool(properties["no_depth_test"]), bool(properties["fixed_size"]), BaseMaterial3D::TextureFilter(int(properties["texture_filter"])), BaseMaterial3D::AlphaAntiAliasing(int(properties["alpha_antialiasing_mode"])), true);
_customize_resource(sprite_3d_material, String());
```

Also, two maybe relevant asides:

1. Rather than mimicking the code inside Sprite3D in the Shader Baker plugin, I wonder if it would be less error-prone to actually expose public functions on Sprite3D that the Shader Baker could call to do this work. There are comments in Shader Baker stating that "this code must match what Sprite3D does internally" - but I could easily see that getting out of sync and causing bugs in the future.

2. The Shader Baker Sprite3D code accounts for Sprite3D shader configurations that exist when the game is compiled, but doesn't account for ones generated at runtime or for Sprite3Ds that are modified at runtime. I wonder if optionally allowing the Shader Baker to enumerate all possible configurations for `StandardMaterial3D::get_material_for_2d` could make sense.

### Steps to reproduce

The provided MRP has a simple scene with a Sprite3D that uses a Region. As a result, the shader used at runtime sets `texture_repeat` to true.

1. Export the project. If you set a breakpoint in `ShaderBakerExportPlugin::_customize_scene`, you should find that the call to `StandardMaterial3D::get_material_for_2d` is generally accurate, but uses `false` for the `p_texture_repeat` argument.
2. At runtime, if you set a breakpoint in `SpriteBase3D::draw_texture_rect`, you'll see that the instance in the scene uses `p_texture_repeat` as `true` because of the region setting.
3. Also, if you set a breakpoint in `ShaderRD::_compile_version_start`, you'll find that a cache miss occurs, despite the shaders being baked ahead of time.
4. If you update the Shader Baker with the code suggested in the issue description, the Shader Baker should bake the version with `texture_repeat` true and you won't get a cache miss anymore.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[godot-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32985815/godot-test.zip)
